Article Title: Ramaiah Group expands its educational legacy with the inauguration of RISM, foundation laying of Nareyana Pragnalaya
Article Text:
Dignitaries at the inauguration of the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management and foundation-laying ceremony for Nareyana Pragnalaya in Bengaluru.

Ramaiah legacy of building a knowledge society

Academic and institutional leaders gathered at the Ramaiah Group event marking the launch of RISM and the foundation laying of Nareyana Pragnalaya.

As India continues to strengthen its position as a knowledge-driven economy, institutions of higher learning are playing an increasingly important role in shaping future-ready talent, advancing research and fostering innovation. Reflecting this vision, the Ramaiah Group of Institutions’ longstanding contribution to education and nation-building came into focus in Bengaluru today, as D.K. Shivakumar, Chief Minister of Karnataka, inaugurated the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management (RISM) and laid the foundation stone for Nareyana Pragnalaya: ‘Abode of Wisdom’, recognising the Group’s significant role in building a knowledge society in India.The ceremony marked an important milestone in the Ramaiah Group’s continuing journey in education and brought together eminent academic and institutional leaders, including Dr. M.R. Jayaram, Chancellor, RISM; Dr. Seetharam, Chairman, Gokula Education Foundation; Dr. Havidan Rodríguez, President, University at Albany, State University of New York; Dr. M.M. Pallam Raju, Member, Board of Management; Prof. B.N. Raghunandan, Chairman, RISM Task Force; and Gurucharan Gollarkeri, IAS (Retd.), Chief Strategy Officer, GEF (Medical), among others.Speaking on the occasion, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appreciated the contribution of the Ramaiah Group of Institutions to education and the development of Bengaluru and Karnataka. He highlighted the role played by the institutions in creating generations of professionals, entrepreneurs and leaders and in contributing to the building of a knowledge-driven society.He also emphasised the importance of educational institutions preparing young people not merely to seek employment, but to become entrepreneurs, innovators and job creators who can contribute meaningfully to the country’s future.Dr. M.R. Jayaram, Chancellor, RISM, highlighted the vision behind the new institution and its focus on global academic engagement, research, innovation and emerging technologies.A key pillar of RISM’s academic vision is its collaboration with the University at Albany, State University of New York. The partnership is intended to provide students with access to global academic expertise, knowledge, research and emerging technologies, while creating opportunities for international exposure and industry-relevant learning.The collaboration brings together the educational legacy of the Ramaiah Group and the global academic strengths of the University at Albany, creating an environment designed to prepare students for a rapidly changing world.Dr. Jayaram also highlighted the significance of Nareyana Pragnalaya, the name given to the new RISM campus for which the foundation stone was laid.Nareyana Pragnalaya means ‘Abode of Wisdom’ and envisions a transformative space where knowledge becomes wisdom, learning inspires discovery, and education shapes enlightened minds.Rooted in timeless values and driven by a vision for tomorrow, the campus is envisioned to nurture intellect, creativity, character and compassion, empowering generations to learn, lead and shape a better world.The foundation laying therefore represents more than the creation of a new campus. It marks the beginning of a new academic environment where knowledge, technology, research and human values come together.The inauguration of the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management and the foundation laying of Nareyana Pragnalaya – ‘Abode of Wisdom’, mark a significant milestone in the continuing educational journey of the Ramaiah Group of Institutions and Gokula Education Foundation.Building on a legacy of contributing to India’s knowledge society, the new initiatives reflect a vision of education that brings together global academic collaboration, emerging technologies, research and innovation, while remaining rooted in the values of wisdom, character and social responsibility. Together, they signal a continued commitment to nurturing future-ready generations equipped not only to navigate a changing world, but also to contribute meaningfully to its future.
Article Summary: Chief Minister of Karnataka, D.K. Shivakumar, inaugurated the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management (RISM) and laid the foundation stone for Nareyana Pragnalaya: ‘Abode of Wisdom’ Dr M.R. Jayaram, Chancellor, RISM, highlighted the vision behind the new institution and its focus on global academic engagement, research, innovation and emerging technologies.

Article Title: A kidney wait since 2024 ends with an Army airlift and a rare double transplant
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An 18-year-old who had spent nearly two years waiting for a kidney, undergoing dialysis twice a week and with no family donor, received not one but two kidneys from a single brain-dead donor on Monday — after the organs were airlifted from Chandimandir to Delhi. Both kidneys were transplanted into Anil Yadav at Safdarjung Hospital, and he is doing well.The donor, 62-year-old Amar Chand, father of an Air Warrior, had undergone coronary artery bypass graft surgery last year and was on dual antiplatelet medication. He later slipped in his bathroom, suffered a head injury and brain haemorrhage, and was declared brain dead at Command Hospital (Western Command), Chandimandir. His organ donation helped save other lives. His liver was transported to Army Hospital (Research & Referral), Delhi, for transplantation, while both corneas were donated to Command Hospital, Chandimandir.His family’s decision to donate his organs set off a race against time. With Army support, the two kidneys were airlifted to Delhi and taken to Safdarjung Hospital, where doctors transplanted both into Anil, who has chronic renal failure.“This is the first en bloc renal transplant at the hospital, in which both kidneys from a donor with marginal renal function were implanted in a single recipient. With a severe shortage of organs nationwide, accepting marginal kidneys can help expand the donor pool and give more dialysis patients, many of whom wait for years, a chance at transplantation,” said Dr Himanshu, Professor & Academic Head, Department of Nephrology, VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital.“The patient is recovering well, with good renal function and urine output.”“The most difficult part of organ donation is counselling a grieving family to say yes within two hours,” said Col Anurag Garg, Transplant Coordinator and Palliative Physician at CHWC. “I have seen this in the Subedar’s family, a Colonel’s wife’s family and Air Warrior Ranbir’s case.”Anil had been waiting for a transplant since 2024, with no donor available in his family. Until Tuesday, twice-weekly haemodialysis had been part of his routine.For a teenager who had spent nearly two years waiting for a donor, the journey from a brain-dead donor in Chandimandir to a transplant table in Delhi took place in time to give him a chance at life beyond dialysis.
Article Summary: Anil Yadav had been waiting for a transplant since 2024, with no donor available in his family. Amar Chand, 62, had undergone coronary artery bypass graft surgery last year and was on dual antiplatelet medication. He later slipped in his bathroom, suffered a head injury and brain haemorrhage, and was declared brain dead. His family’s decision to donate his organs set off a race against time.

Article Title: 'This is treason': Rahul Gandhi revives 'vote chori' charge after report of rift within EC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday revived his "vote chori" charge against the Election Commission and accused election officials of committing "treason".In a post on X, Rahul said, "I am telling the EC and election officials clearly: What you are doing is wrong. This is treason, this is against the country. Do not forget that. The time will come when we will catch you. You will not be able to escape."His remarks came after an Indian Express report claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections to the poll panel's actions at least 14 times over the past 10 months during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The report said the commissioners had flagged issues relating to the addition and deletion of voters as well as the handling of voter data.Senior Congress leaders KC Venugopal and P Chidambaram also stepped up their attack on the poll panel following the report.Chidambaram said the opposition had already contended that several decisions concerning the SIR were wrong and questioned how Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's view could become the decision of the Commission if the two Election Commissioners had taken a contrary position."The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that if the decision-making process is flawed or wrong, the decision will also be flawed or wrong. The opposition has contended that many decisions concerning SIR were wrong. Now, it is revealed that the decision-making process was also wrong," Chidambaram said."If two ECs have taken a contrary view, how could the CEC make his view the 'decision' of the ECI? All decisions of the ECI in recent years should be reviewed by a Parliamentary Committee. Meanwhile, the SIR process should be suspended immediately all over the country," he added.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal also targeted CEC Gyanesh Kumar and demanded his removal."There is no doubt remaining. Mr Gyanesh Kumar has no right to remain in office. How the hell can one man, acting on His Master's orders, strike off names at whim? How can he sideline fellow Constitutional officers to only take blatantly illegal steps that put our democracy in danger?" Venugopal said."The right to vote is an essential Constitutional power given to every citizen, the fundamental bedrock of our democracy. If it is to be taken away, due process must be followed with utmost probity," he added.The Election Commission, however, rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the SIR and said all decisions related to the exercise were taken unanimously.Officials told news agency PTI that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling, but these did not amount to disagreement with the final decisions taken by the Commission.EC sources said all decisions of the Commission, including those relating to the SIR, had the approval of Sandhu, Joshi and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Officials also pointed out that the law governing the Election Commission, as well as a Supreme Court judgment, provides that decisions should, as far as possible, be taken unanimously. Where unanimity is not possible, the majority view prevails.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses election officials of committing "treason" Congress leaders KC Venugopal and P Chidambaram also step up attack on the poll panel. Election Commission rejects reports of differences over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR)

As Kolkata’s residential landscape continues to evolve, emerging micro-markets are gaining prominence as homebuyers increasingly seek a combination of connectivity, convenience and well-developed social infrastructure. The Southern EM Bypass corridor, in particular, has witnessed a decade-long transformation from a peripheral suburb into one of the city’s most aspirational residential addresses, supported by expanding metro and suburban rail connectivity, dual EM Bypass access, and a maturing ecosystem of schools, hospitals and retail destinations. Against this backdrop, Srijan Realty, one of Eastern India’s most established residential developers, today announced the launch of Orizon, a 702-unit residential community spread across 8.3 acres off the Southern EM Bypass in Jagaddal, South Kolkata.Located on B.C. Roy Road in Jagaddal, with two access points off the Southern EM Bypass roughly 400 metres and 750 metres apart, Orizon comprises six high-rise towers ranging from 17 to 23 storeys, housing 702 three-bedroom residences sized between approximately 1,208 and 1,650 square feet. Roughly 80 percent of the 8.3-acre site — 85 percent including podium-level landscaping, has been kept open, an unusually low-density ratio for a development of this scale so close to the city. Shahid Khudiram Metro Station is roughly14 minutes away, with Sonarpur railway station around 15 minutes; Spencer’s, Wood Square Mall and Southwinds Galleria are all within a six-minute drive.Orizon’s design philosophy takes its name from the word “horizon,” built around the idea that space, light and an unobstructed view are increasingly scarce commodities in a city that has grown denser over the past two decades. Residences feature terrace-style and standing balconies intended to maximise natural light and cross-ventilation, while the project’s golden façade, visible from the EM Bypass — is conceived as a visual landmark along the corridor.Despite its dual EM Bypass access and proximity to South Kolkata’s commercial nodes, the development has been planned to function as a self-contained green enclave, insulated from the congestion typically associated with high-density urban corridors. Schools including BDM International and Narayana, along with healthcare providers such as Apollo Hospital’s upcoming campus, Peerless Hospital and RN Tagore Hospital, are within a 20-minute radius.At the centre of the development sits a roughly 33,000-square-foot clubhouse featuring an infinity-edge swimming pool, jacuzzi and dedicated kids’ pool, alongside a 21,000-square-foot podium-level garden anchoring a sports arena with facilities for tennis, basketball, pickleball and badminton. Indoor offerings extend to a gymnasium, yoga and meditation studio, squash court, co-working space, home theatre, library, and a dedicated senior citizens’ lounge, amenities the developer says are designed to serve every age group within a single community rather than cater narrowly to one demographic.A defining feature of Orizon is its barrier-free design, incorporating wheelchair access ramps, lift cabins wide enough to accommodate wheelchairs, Braille and voice-enabled lift controls, accessible toilets and designated accessible parking throughout common areas. Srijan Realty positions this not as a regulatory minimum but as a forward-looking response to India’s multigenerational households, where ageing parents, differently abled family members and young children increasingly share a single home and require equal, independent access to shared spaces.Orizon has been pre-certified for IGBC Platinum design, India’s highest green building rating, with features including rainwater harvesting, solar power for common areas, low-flow water fixtures, energy-efficient LED lighting, organic waste management, and EV charging infrastructure. Buildings certified to this standard typically deliver 20 to 30 percent energy savings and 30 to 50 percent water savings compared with conventional construction."Orizon reflects how we believe Kolkata wants to live today. Homebuyers are no longer choosing between space and connectivity, or between design and responsibility - they expect all of it together. Southern EM Bypass has moved past being an emerging corridor - it is now one of South Kolkata's defining growth engines, and we have been part of that story for over a decade.We have built Orizon as a community first, planned around low-density living, open space, and lifestyle infrastructure that we believe will hold its value well beyond the next market cycle, with inclusivity and sustainability designed into its foundations rather than added on at the end”, said Dinesh Agarwal, Director, Srijan Realty, reflecting on the vision behind the project.Rera number: Phase I - WBRERA/P/SOU/2026/004474 |NOTE: The information contained herein is indicative and for promotional purposes. RERA registration details available at [insert RERA number]. Prospective buyers are advised to review all legal and regulatory documentation before making investment decisions.
Article Summary: Orizon is a 702-unit residential community spread across 8.3 acres off the Southern EM Bypass in Jagaddal, South Kolkata. The development has been planned to function as a self-contained green enclave, insulated from the congestion typically associated with high-density urban corridors. Srijan Realty, one of Eastern India’s most established residential developers, is the developer.

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday said the party stood firmly with the people of Ladakh in their demand for meaningful constitutional safeguards, including Sixth Schedule status, to protect the Union Territory’s land, employment opportunities, fragile environment, culture and identity.In a post on X, Kharge said four young people were shot dead in Leh a year ago during protests demanding democratic and constitutional rights for the people of Ladakh."A year ago, four young people were shot in Leh during the agitation for the Democratic and Constitutional rights of the people of Ladakh. NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying all decisions related to the exercise were taken "unanimously".The poll body clarified that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling, but these did not amount to disagreement with the final decisions taken by the Commission.The clarification came after an Indian Express report triggered a row by claiming that the two Election Commissioners had raised objections to the Commission's decisions 14 times over the past 10 months during the SIR exercise.EC sources told PTI that all decisions taken by the Election Commission, including those related to the SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as well as Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Responding to queries, officials said Sandhu and Joshi had flagged issues related to the deletion of names from electoral rolls in various states and the handling of voter data.Officials also pointed out that the law governing the Election Commission, as well as a Supreme Court judgment, provides that decisions should, as far as possible, be taken unanimously. Where unanimity is not possible, the majority view prevails.Meanwhile, opposition sharpened its attack on the Election Commission over the SIR, claiming it was meant to target electors not aligned to the BJP and its allies.Urging the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognizance of the issue, several opposition parties attacked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and accused him of becoming a puppet of those in power.In a social media post, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the poll panel of hatching a conspiracy to "wipe out democracy.""This is an extremely serious news that in the past 10 months, 2 Election Commissioners have registered their objections 14 times against the Election Commission's wrong decisions," Akhilesh said."This directly means that all Election Commissioners are not able to perform their rightful duties. If the members of an independent body do not have the freedom to carry out just actions or if there is no hearing of theirs, then these are extremely fatal and dangerous circumstances for democracy. For some people to betray democracy by becoming puppets of those in power is a grave constitutional crime. This is nothing less than a conspiracy to wipe out democracy," he added.Mamata Trinamool Congress (MTMC) also slammed CEC Kumar and said that the opposition should reintroduce the impeachment motion against Kumar in Parliament."Five months ago, more than 60 Rajya Sabha Members of Parliament... when only 50 were needed, wrote to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha moving a motion to remove the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, that was five months ago. Now today, after this big news break that two Election Commissioners objected to many of the CEC's actions, it's time to bring out the Rajya Sabha motion to impeach the CEC and save democracy," MTMC's Derek O' O'Brien said.The issue is likely to escalate further as leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been vehement in his criticism of the Election Commission and the SIR process, alleging that it has resulted in the denial of voting rights.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has rejected reports of differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) The poll body clarified that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi did raise concerns over some aspects of voter roll deletion and database handling.

Article Title: PM Modi likely to visit Canada in December to lock in trade deal: Canadian PM Carney
Article Text:
PM Modi and Canadian PM Mark Carney (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada in December to seal the trade deal between New Delhi and Ottawa, Canadian PM Mark Carney said on Tuesday.Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Carney said that the relationship between India and Canada is "exceptionally important" and claimed that both countries are looking to reach a trade deal by the end of the year."We're making good progress in our trade negotiations with India. It is an exceptionally important relationship, on many, many levels. People-to-people levels, security levels and also trade and economic," Carney said."He (PM Modi) will be visiting Canada around that time. I very much look forward to hosting him," he added.This comes after Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal said that India and Canada have agreed to fast-track negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership, with the next round of talks scheduled to begin on October 5.Goyal said he had concluded the fourth round of negotiations for the proposed trade agreement with his Canadian counterpart, minister of international trade Maninder Sidhu, in Mumbai last week."I have concluded the fourth round of negotiations for the Canada trade deal with my counterpart Mr Maninder Sidhu in Mumbai on Friday. Very productive discussions and both sides have resolved to fast-track negotiations, in view of which our team is now slated to go for the fifth round," he said."Fifth of October. So you can see that as the progress is taking shape, the speed of negotiations with Canada is also improving. Let's see, the next 90 days should be a very defining period in the Canada-India relationship," the minister said.India and Canada have discussed a comprehensive trade pact for more than a decade. Negotiations were formally relaunched in March 2022, with the two sides also pursuing an Early Progress Trade Agreement as an interim step. Nine negotiating rounds were held between 2022 and 2023 before the process was paused in August 2023 amid a period of strain in bilateral relations.Trade talks between India and Canada restarted during the G20 summit in 2025 as both countries saw a thaw in diplomatic relations post the standoff with former Canadian PM Justin Trudeau who had blamed India for the killing of designated terrorist Hardeep Nijjar in Canada.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada in December to seal the trade deal between New Delhi and Ottawa. Canadian PM Mark Carney said that the relationship between India and Canada is "exceptionally important" Carney claimed that both countries are looking to reach a trade deal by the end of the year.

Article Title: NSE IPO listing: National Stock Exchange of India to debut on September 24; check GMP & other details
Article Text:

NSE IPO subscription

NSE IPO GMP Today

About NSE

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

NSE IPO listing: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) is set to debut on the stock market on September 24, 2026. The shares are scheduled to begin trading on the BSE. With the listing now just a day away, the grey market is indicating a premium of about 2.4%. The premium has moderated from around 4% earlier, pointing to a potentially limited gain over the issue price at the time of listing.As the NSE listing approaches, investors will be watching movements in the grey market premium, the broader market mood and participation from institutional investors. These factors will be closely followed as the exchange prepares for its debut on the BSE.The Rs 22,562 crore public issue consists entirely of an offer for sale (OFS). A total of 12.64 crore shares are being offered by existing shareholders. As NSE itself is not selling any shares in the issue, the exchange will not receive money raised through the IPO. The proceeds will instead go to the shareholders participating in the OFS.NSE had set the price band for the issue at Rs 1,700-1,785 per share and fixed the lot size at eight shares. At the current grey market premium of 2.4%, the implied listing price works out to around Rs 1,828 per share, compared with the upper end of the IPO price band at Rs 1,785.Subscription to the IPO began on September 17 and ended on September 21, with the issue drawing strong interest from investors across categories. Overall, the IPO was subscribed 5.71 times. The retail investor portion received 1.39 times subscription, while the non-institutional investor (NII) segment was subscribed 6.55 times. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) put in the strongest demand, with their portion receiving 12.68 times subscription.Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Ltd., Morgan Stanley India Company Pvt. Ltd. and HSBC Securities & Capital Markets (India) Pvt. Ltd. have been appointed as the book-running lead managers for the issue. Link Intime India Pvt. Ltd. is serving as the registrar.The grey market premium (GMP) for the NSE IPO is currently around Rs 43 per share, equivalent to 2.4%, according to an ET report. This is lower than the roughly 4% premium seen earlier.The current premium is calculated against the upper end of the IPO price band, which is Rs 1,785 per share.The National Stock Exchange is India's largest stock exchange and operates an integrated platform covering trading, clearing, listing, data services and index licensing. Its offerings include the cash market, futures and options, mutual funds, commodity derivatives, currency derivatives, the wholesale debt market and interest rate futures.NSE has remained India's leading exchange by cash market turnover as well as equity derivatives turnover from FY01 through FY26. As of June 2026, the exchange had 132.4 million unique registered investors and 1,328 trading members. It had 3,005 listed entities, with the market capitalization of these entities at around Rs 474.1 trillion.
Article Summary: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) is set to debut on the stock market on September 24, 2026. The shares are scheduled to begin trading on the BSE. With the listing now just a day away, the grey market is indicating a premium of about 2.4%.

The court contrasted this with Greater Noida, saying the latter was planned with the next 30-40 years in mind.The observations came while the top court was hearing a plea challenging the Karnataka High Court's decision upholding the state's Premium Floor Area Ratio (FAR) scheme.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, issued notice on the plea filed by the Citizens Action Forum.The bench, however, clarified that the additional FAR available under the scheme should not be used to regularise illegal construction.Chief Justice Surya Kant said there was no visible improvement or addition to the basic infrastructure of the township, such as roads, sewer lines and bus flyovers, despite the additional construction capacity."We have seen in Gurugram how this system collapses if any natural calamity comes.Because, without adding to this infrastructure, you are burdening the size of the plot with multiple storeys," the CJI said.He said the situation was different in Greater Noida because the city had been planned keeping the next 30-40 years in mind.The observations came amid arguments over whether Bengaluru's existing infrastructure can support additional construction allowed under the Premium FAR scheme.The Premium FAR scheme allows property owners to purchase additional construction rights beyond the ordinarily permissible FAR by paying prescribed premium charges. The stated objective is to facilitate vertical development and generate revenue for urban local bodies.FAR refers to the ratio of a building's total floor area to the size of the plot on which it stands.Senior advocate Aditya Sondhi, appearing for the Citizens Action Forum, argued that road width had effectively become the main criterion for granting Premium FAR, despite existing pressure on Bengaluru's parking, water, electricity and other infrastructure.Justice Bagchi also referred to Bengaluru's traffic problems, saying the city has a "traffic nightmare" and that this was a serious concern raised by the petitioner.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state authorities, said the overall additional FAR remained capped at 0.6. He also said existing setback and parking requirements continued to apply and that developers could not simply purchase additional FAR without meeting parking and other regulatory requirements.Mehta said the money collected under the scheme would go into a dedicated fund for civic infrastructure.A key issue before the bench was whether the Premium FAR scheme could be used to regularise unauthorised construction.Sondhi questioned how the new scheme differed from the earlier Akrama-Sakrama scheme, under which unauthorised constructions were legalised. He told the court that a provision in the Greater Bengaluru Authority Act allowed Premium FAR to be used for regularising existing illegal constructions.Mehta rejected the contention and gave an assurance that unauthorised construction covered by the Akrama-Sakrama scheme would not be regularised under the Premium FAR scheme."It has nothing to do with that. Kindly record my statement. It is completely different. You can also pass directions to this effect," Mehta said.He argued that urban space was limited and vertical growth was the way forward, adding that cities were increasingly moving towards vertical development.The Supreme Court asked the Bengaluru authorities to file their response to the plea within four weeks.The case challenges the Karnataka High Court's June 15 judgment upholding the constitutional validity of the Premium FAR scheme. The high court had dismissed petitions arguing that the scheme violated property rights and reduced the value of Transferable Development Rights (TDRs).The Premium FAR scheme was introduced under Section 18-B of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961. The high court had held that it did not violate Articles 14, 21 or 300A of the Constitution.The NGO had argued that Premium FAR allowed developers to purchase additional building rights at rates significantly below the market cost of TDRs, thereby undermining TDRs secured by landowners as compensation for land.The high court rejected the argument, holding that a state policy resulting in fluctuations in property values would not by itself make the policy violative of Article 300A.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says urban system in Gurugram collapses during rains because adequate investment was not made in infrastructure. Court contrasted this with Greater Noida, saying the latter was planned with the next 30-40 years in mind. Chief Justice Surya Kant said there was no visible improvement or addition to the basic infrastructure of the township.

NEW DELHI: The BJP is set to have the numbers on its side in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, with the party-led alliance expected to win eight of the 10 seats going to polls in the state. The Samajwadi Party could take the remaining two seats, based on the current strength of parties in the assembly.The Election Commission on Tuesday announced polls for 12 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. A candidate needs around 37 votes to win a Rajya Sabha seat.The BJP can comfortably win seven seats, while the SP-Congress combine can secure two.The contest for the 10th seat could be closer, with the BJP-led alliance starting with around 31 votes against around 29 for the SP-Congress side.The polls could also mark the end of the BSP's representation in Parliament. Mayawati's party has no member in the Lok Sabha and its only MLA in Uttar Pradesh, Uma Shankar Singh, died in August. The term of BSP's lone Rajya Sabha member, Ramji Gautam, ends in November.Gautam is among the nine Uttar Pradesh members whose terms are ending. The others are Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brijlal, B L Verma and Seema Dwivedi, and SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav.Puri's continuation in the Union Cabinet will depend on whether the BJP nominates him for another Rajya Sabha term.The 10th Uttar Pradesh seat was held by former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma. It became vacant earlier this month after Sharma resigned from the Rajya Sabha following his appointment as lieutenant governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.The BSP had managed to retain its Rajya Sabha presence in 2020 after the BJP fielded only eight candidates for 10 seats. The SP had then alleged an understanding between the BJP and BSP.In Uttarakhand, BJP Rajya Sabha member Naresh Bansal's term is ending. Article Title: Shouldn’t punish for refusing to sing ‘Vande Mataram’: Supreme Court
Article Text:
SC disagreed with the suggestion that the recognition of all six stanzas was not in concord with a ‘secular’ Constitution.

Courts can’t dictate what national song should be: SC

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to examine the legality of penal consequences if a person does not sing the national song due to religious beliefs or conscientious objection, but declined to adjudicate whether ‘Vande Mataram’ should comprise two or six stanzas, saying it was best left to Parliament’s wisdom.The court was hearing a petition by Carnatic vocalist T M Krishna objecting to recital of the complete version of the national song on the ground that its last four stanzas invoked Hindu goddesses which may offend the religious beliefs of some communities. The amended law stipulates punishment of up to three years in jail for disrupting or preventing rendition of the song.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the field was occupied by SC’s Aug 1986 Bijoe Emmanuel vs Kerala judgment that no one could be penalised for not singing the national anthem if he showed respect to it by standing in silence.Seeking the Centre’s reply in two weeks, the bench said, “nobody’s Article 25 rights or the right of a conscientious objector should be violated”.It said the Bijoe Emmanuel case ruling had never been challenged and was still the law of the land. The Centre must consider the issue raised in the PIL from that perspective, it said.The bench added that if a conscientious objector did not sing one or all stanzas of the national song, he would not be subjected to criminal prosecution.Appearing for Krishna, senior advocate S Muralidhar argued that ‘Vande Mataram’ must be confined to two stanzas, as done by Congress Working Committee in 1937 due to strong opposition by Muslims, whose faith does not permit idol worship.The hearing was marked by the bench disagreeing with the suggestion that the recognition of all six stanzas as the national song was not in concord with a “secular” Constitution and a heated exchange between solicitor general Tu-shar Mehta and Muralidhar.Muralidhar’s argument that the law-making process, where Parliament made singing of all six stanzas of Vande Mataram mandatory, was not inclusive as it did not fully accommodate public opinion had Mehta angrily retorting that law-making could not be made subservient to the “diktat of Naxalite ideas”.Justice Bagchi was sceptical of the argument that singing all six stanzas would undermine the constitutional mandate of secularism, which is a sine qua non for constitutional governance.Justice Bagchi told Muralidhar, “Nothing can be more strong or positive secularism than the US constitution. But the American national anthem uses the word ‘God’. The national song, not national anthem, paying homage to a particular form of God will not perhaps impact secularism. But your point is about whether someone who is a conscientious objector can be subjected to penal consequences. We will examine it.”Muralidhar said all six stanzas were thrust upon people after 80 years and not singing it invited penal consequences. “That is what is most worrying,” he said.The SC said, “Penal consequences we will examine. But the state is best suited to declare what the national song is and articulate national aspirations. If these kinds of issues are debated, then this would be the most unfortunate thing for the nation. Courts cannot dictate what the national song should be.”Mehta said the petition was meant to create sensationalism and persuaded the court not to issue notice while assuring that Centre would file a response.The bench said, “We may not issue notice. But the law of the land as declared by SC (in Bijoe Emanuel case) governs the acts of the state. That declaration has not been questioned. There is no dispute as to what the national song is. It is for the democratically elected state to decide what the national song is, four stanzas or two stanzas. But nobody’s Article 25 rights or the right of a conscientious objector should be violated.It is not for the court to second-guess the national sentiment or aspirations associated with ‘Vande Mataram’.”Mehta said it was not for the petitioner to decide whether the national song should be of two or six stanzas. “Those who could not stall the amendment to Prevention of Insults to National Honours Act in Parliament are now bringing the issue to the court,” he added.
Article Summary: Supreme Court agrees to examine the legality of penal consequences if a person does not sing the national song due to religious beliefs or conscientious objection. The court declined to adjudicate whether ‘Vande Mataram’ should comprise two or six stanzas, saying it was best left to Parliament.

Article Title: India teams up with EU, Canada & others to defend multilateralism; EAM says rules must be scrupulously followed

India joined the EU, Canada, Australia and several other countries in co-sponsoring a declaration expressing a joint commitment to multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity, while expressing concern over escalating conflicts, trade disruption, power politics protectionism and coercion.The declaration followed the announcement of a new initiative titled Partners for Multilateralism (P4M) on the margins of the UN General Assembly that aims to make multilateral bodies more “representative, effective, legitimate and trusted” through middle-power cooperation, amid growing fragmentation and violations of international law.Drawing attention to geopolitical tensions, conflicts and extreme competition, foreign minister S Jaishankar said multilateralism will be best served when international law, rules, and norms are scrupulously observed.Other declaration co-sponsors included Brazil, Barbados and Kenya, making P4M a diverse group of countries that bridges – unlike the G7 and BRICS - the gap between the West and Global South. After the co-sponsors, 16 other countries signed off on the declaration that flagged increasing use of economic interdependence as a source of leverage, disrupting trade, supply chains, investment and development finance in messages directed at both US and China.The declaration stressed reform of multilateral institutions, including the UN, to promote fair trade, prevent conflicts and protect rule of law, while backing fair, open, resilient, predictable and inclusive economic cooperation, including more diversified and resilient global supply chains.The declaration said that the multilateral system founded on the UN Charter remained indispensable, as it had helped provide a framework for peace, decolonisation, prosperity, and human dignity. However, the declaration also said that it must now respond to a world that is more interconnected and complex, more contested and more multipolar.“We affirm the need to uphold and enforce the rules, principles and commitments that remain essential to international order, while renewing and reforming the multilateral system so that it is more effective, representative, inclusive and fit for purpose,” said the declaration, while stressing the joint commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, peaceful settlement of disputes and prohibition of the threat or use of force.The inaugural meeting was co-hosted by European Council President Antonio Costa who said that the P4M will serve as a global network for dialogue, coalition-building and practical cooperation, helping us coordinate our response to shared challenges, with the UN at its core.As he underlined the need for multilateralism to assert itself strongly in these times, Jaishankar also pointed to the issue of terrorism. “The future of peace and international security, of climate action and climate justice, of emerging technologies and development finance ,of countering terrorism and strengthening supply chain, and of ensuring disaster resilience and preparing for pandemics, all depend on a will to cooperate,” he said.The minister also flagged the 4F crises of fuel, food, fertilizer and finance cannot be left to itself, saying where new capabilities and concerns arise, there is a very powerful case for frameworks and guardrails.“Where there is a threat of chokepoints dominance and disruption, de-risking and diversifying must be encouraged. And where there is a compelling cause or a powerful case, the like-minded must have the confidence to come together,” said Jaishankar, stressing the need for reformed multilateralism.
Article Summary: India joined the EU, Canada, Australia and several other countries in co- sponsoring a declaration. The declaration expressed a joint commitment to multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity. It expressed concern over escalating conflicts, trade disruption, power politics protectionism and coercion.

Article Title: Exorbitant pricing of drugs is ‘extortion': Supreme Court
Article Text:
If this is not extortion, then what is it, says SC on allowing retailers to overprice drugs

Bench expressed surprise at the huge disparity in pricing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Expressing shock over patients and their families being fleeced by pharma companies and retail medicine sellers, Supreme Court on Tuesday said the exorbitant prices charged was nothing but “dacoity” in broad daylight and questioned the govt’s silence on the pressing issue faced by citizens.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said price fixation of medicines was very important as people were being forced to sell their assets and ornaments to purchase medicines and suggested that all medicines should be brought under the purview of the price control mechanism and be made available under govt-sponsored Jan Aushadhi Kendras. Referring to a cancer drug without naming it, the bench said the pharma company supplied it to retailers at Rs 2,770 but it was sold to patients at an MRP of Rs 27,000.“There are medicines, essential medicines for cancer, which the MRP is 27,000 and the PTR (price to retailer) is Rs 2,700. That’s absolute rampage, carnage, broad daylight dacoity. How can a patient be cheated for a medicine, which the manufacturer sells to the retailer at Rs 2,700 and the MRP is printed at Rs 27,000? It is ten times. It is very surprising that the authorities who are supposed to take a decision on this are absolutely silent.We don’t need to spell out the reason for that,” the bench said.Additional solicitor general K M Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, told the bench that the govt was not taking an adversarial approach in the matter and it would remain the govt’s endeavour to make medicines available to all. But the bench interrupted him and pointed out that the issue was not about availability but about making them available at a reasonable price.“If that is not extortion, then what is it? People sell their houses, sell their ornaments for getting medicines... Price fixation is very important and all medicines should be brought under price fixation policy. If all medicines are important, then why keep some medicines out of it?” the bench asked. The court was hearing PILs filed by SC advocate K C Jain and Agra-based doctor Sanjay Kulshresthra seeking the court’s intervention on price fixation of medicines.The petitioners placed before the court bills to demonstrate how drugs were being overpriced by pharma companies or by printing a much higher MRP than their actual retail price in the open market, which allowed retailers to sell the medicines at 10-16 times their actual cost.Giving an example, Kulshresthra told the court that the MRP of an antibiotic named Tigebex 50 mg was Rs 5,635 and was sold at that price in corporate hospitals but the same was being sold in the open market at just Rs 350.“In other words, the hospital is charging 16 times its actual retail cost in the market,” he said.The bench expressed surprise at the huge disparity in pricing and said, “Why this disparity at all? A medicine which is, as a matter of fact, sold by the manufacturer to the retailer at 10% of its MRP, why has it got this high MRP? Why should there be such disparity? It is a clear cut case of fraud on the face of it.”Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for pharma companies, said they were not the ones making money out of it and sought time to place data before the court, which was allowed.
Article Summary: Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said price fixation of medicines was very important. They suggested that all medicines should be brought under the purview of the price control mechanism and be made available under govt-sponsored Jan Aushadhi Kendras. Bench expressed surprise at the huge disparity in pricing.

Article Title: 'Non-application of mind': Court sets aside order refusing probe in Sonia Gandhi electoral roll case
Article Text:

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Monday allowed a revision plea challenging a magistrate's order refusing to probe the allegation that Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's name was included in the electoral roll in 1980, three years before she acquired Indian citizenship.Special Judge Vishal Gogne delivered the judgment two days after deferring it. He quashed the order as "non-speaking" or an order that does not explain the reasons behind a judge's conclusion."The impugned order suffers from a manifest error in law on account of non-compliance with Section 175(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), inter alia, not hearing the submissions of the police officer concerned and non-calling of a status report from the police station concerned," the Special Judge noted."The 'non-speaking' nature of the order was evident as the magistrate did not consider the twin options under law of directing the registration of an FIR or alternatively conducting proceedings under the BNSS, and instead of considering the core aspect of whether the complaint disclosed the commission of a cognisable offence, the magistrate digressed towards the issue of citizenship," he added.The court remanded the matter back to the magistrate to pass a reasoned order after hearing fresh arguments.The matter has been posted for further proceedings on September 29.In September last year, advocate Vikas Tripathi filed a plea in a Delhi magistrate's court seeking action against Sonia Gandhi, claiming her name appeared on the electoral rolls three years before she became an Indian citizen in 1983. The plea had sought a police investigation into what it terms a possible case of forgery.The application had pointed to documents suggesting Sonia Gandhi took Indian citizenship on April 30, 1983. Yet, her name allegedly appeared as a voter in the New Delhi constituency roll in 1980, was deleted in 1982, and re-entered in April 1983 after she formally became an Indian national.Tripathi's plea was dismissed on September 11, 2025, prompting him to approach a higher court.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah Tuesday said India’s war on drugs will now be waged at the district level, establishing the local administrative unit as the primary battlefield to dismantle illicit networks.Inaugurating the third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) heads of states and UTs in Delhi, Shah outlined the district-centric strategy, giving an operational break-up for targeting trafficking operations with a ground-up approach. “Under the new framework, districts nationwide will be categorised into three distinct clusters based on their role in the narcotics supply chain — drug manufacturing or entry points, transportation corridors, and high-consumption districts,” Shah said.Correspondingly, enforcement agencies will execute a simultaneous, three-level attack against drug cartels, identifying their primary touchpoints, inter-state distribution systems and local sales networks operating within individual districts. State police forces have been instructed to integrate the conversion of raw information into actionable intelligence directly into their daily organisational culture.To ensure tangible results, Shah mandated an immediate shift across all state ANTFs, seeking a transition from routine meetings to active missions, from simple reporting to proven results, from a seizure-centric mindset to total network dismantling and from initial case registration to final court conviction.Reiterating India’s resolute stance to not allow a single gram of drugs to enter or exit the country, Shah expressed confidence that this synchronised grassroots strategy will secure complete victory and achieve a ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat’ by 2029.Shah also directed police departments to abandon surface-level drug seizures in favour of comprehensive backward and forward investigations, financial auditing and tracing of digital links to choke cartel funding. He emphasised the aggressive application of PIT-NDPS Act alongside tight coordination with public prosecutors from investigation to conviction.On emerging global threats, Shah called for specialised ‘out-of-the-box’ officer teams in every state to tackle synthetic drugs, precursor chemical diversion, dark-net markets, crypto transactions and dead-drop delivery systems. Furthermore, he mandated a dedicated campaign to deport and blacklist foreign drug offenders operating in India, while tracking and extraditing overseas fugitives supplying drugs into the country.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah Tuesday said India’s war on drugs will now be waged at the district level. Shah outlined the district-centric strategy at the third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) heads of states and UTs in Delhi.

Article Title: UPI MDR will fund innovation, protect small merchants: NPCI’s Dilip Asbe
Article Text:
The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed.

Why this sudden move to charge MDR on UPI, and how did you decide on the Rs 2,000 threshold and the 0.4% MDR? Will you review the scheme periodically?

How much is expected to be collected in the first year, around Rs 15,000 crore?

What is the rationale for the charge given that the government can easily foot a bill of Rs 20,000 crore, as it is a tiny fraction of its budget, especially when it spends thousands of crores on non-merit subsidies? Why can't banks, NPCI or RBI bear the burden?

What is being done to ensure that customers are not burdened with MDR? Also, is NPCI proposing a relook at GST?

How do you propose to utilise the money to develop the market? Do you see banks and other service providers offering loyalty points for UPI transactions, as is the case with credit cards?

Will there be a check on merchants and consumers splitting transactions to avoid MDR over Rs 2,000?

The new system has created confusion around several aspects of the scheme...

How do you respond to allegations that the decision was taken under US pressure?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Why is the P2PM limit so low?

The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed. In an interview with TOI, Dilip Asbe, MD & CEO, explains how the new fee structure protects small transactions while charging larger merchants, who already pay fees on card payments. Besides, there are a host of exemptions aimed at shielding consumers and small merchants. NPCI expects Rs 13,000-15,000 crore in the first year, with 5% of this being ploughed back to support small merchants, while periodic reviews will assess the model.UPI P2M was charged from inception, and we followed the global model of keeping P2P free and P2M at reasonable cost recovery, much lower than the prescribed MDR for debit and credit cards, net banking or wallets. The government's decision on zero MDR in 2020 helped UPI expand rapidly among merchants during the Covid period. In the last four years, the UPI ecosystem — namely NPCI, banks, fintech start-ups and industry bodies such as the Payments Council of India and IBA — has been seeking a review to ensure a self-sustainable system that can create long-term value for the country, citizens and merchants. UPI growth has slowed, and India remains under-penetrated compared with China and Brazil, where almost 90% of the adult population uses digital payments every day, versus 40% in our case.So, we need investment to expand digital payments, especially among the poor.The charges were finalised primarily keeping in mind the costs incurred by various players to process UPI transactions. Instead of a fixed-fee model, which would penalise low-ticket transactions, we opted for percentage-based charges so that high-ticket transactions with margins can contribute the majority of the MDR. Certain categories with high ticket sizes but lower margins were kept at a flat Rs 5 irrespective of the ticket size, to continue driving adoption. If you review the rates, they are almost at par with global rates for QR-based payments, which are charged similarly without making any exceptions, while these charges remain much lower than those for debit or credit card transactions currently paid by large merchants.It may take some time for the system to settle down. Maybe, in the first year, we will collect Rs 13,000-15,000 crore, of which 5% will be allocated to the small merchant fund to incentivise digital-payment growth among small merchants. We will soon release the guidelines on this.The idea is not to burden small players, as we expect over 80% of the MDR charges to come from businesses with over Rs 1,000 crore turnover. Most of them are already accepting cards and paying much higher MDR on cards under the current construct. There are competing demands on public funds, and this is the best way to make the ecosystem sustainable, grow and innovate without depending on subsidies.NPCI is a not-for-profit entity; all its profits are reinvested in creating infrastructure, reserves for settlement guarantees, innovation and resilience. NPCI needs to not only survive but thrive for the next 100 years.Banks continue to make substantial investments in maintaining and scaling the UPI ecosystem, with annual expenditure often exceeding Rs 2,000 crore for most large banks. At the same time, a Rs 5,000 cash withdrawal can often be substituted by 50 to 100 UPI transactions, highlighting the scale and efficiency of digital payments. While the transition from cash to digital payments has undoubtedly delivered savings through lower cash-handling and ATM-servicing costs, banks also incur significant costs in building and operating resilient, secure and scalable UPI payment infrastructure.Over the last six years, the overall ecosystem has invested over Rs 75,000 crore to maintain and grow the UPI ecosystem without much cost recovery. These investments and innovations will benefit the country in the long run.Running the UPI ecosystem requires around Rs 21,000 crore annually, and we have sought to protect small merchants and low-value payments to help smaller firms raise capital and invest. The idea is also to have more players to increase competition. As a result, person-to-person transactions and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000, with no upper cap on cumulative or repeat transactions, all recurring payments or AutoPay, and small individual merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month into their own accounts will not face any MDR. Since most of the MDR will be generated from merchants who already accept card payments, the consumer price is already factored into MDR charges, or else we would have seen merchants offering major discounts for UPI and RuPay debit card transactions over the last six years. We have prohibited platform fees and merchants charging customers. We plan to review it periodically along with the ecosystem. On GST, I have no comments to offer since this decision will be made by the finance ministry and GST Council. However, major large merchants will claim an input tax credit for the GST paid.The objective of these charges is to ensure the ecosystem thrives, becomes self-sustainable, and is able to innovate and create value that, in turn, grows UPI. Today, we observe that payment methods with good cost recovery tend to have better innovation and features. For example, EMIs, rewards and discount offers help grow merchant sales, particularly in categories such as electronics. Once cost recovery starts, the ecosystem will create a major drive to onboard new consumers and merchants, install more sound boxes and increase activity in under-penetrated geographies and categories through digitalisation. Amid evolving times and landscapes, it will also allow the ecosystem to invest proactively in cybersecurity and resilience.Any policy that has a ceiling or a floor has these second-order effects. If the consumer is ready to participate in splitting the transactions based on a merchant's request, we do not foresee any harm in this and, accordingly, no upper cap on such transactions has been defined. We believe this may, at best, be a short-term phenomenon and that consumer experience will ultimately win in the long run. What we have seen globally and in India is that it is primarily the consumer's choice that drives digital payments.Yes, but we are working with industry bodies and ecosystem participants to provide clarity. For example, some people have interpreted the no-MDR limit below Rs 2,000 as a daily cap and not a per-transaction limit, which is not the case.The USTR has a reference to a UPI market-share cap of 30%, as well as NCMC standards access to other competing international schemes, which is a fair and factual point, and we believe it must be a country's prerogative to make that decision. We didn't find any reference to charges or MDR, and, as I said above, it benefits competing companies to keep it free.This is more like an intermediate step for a merchant moving from receiving money via standard P2P to graduating into a proper P2M merchant so that it gets the support of a sound box, POS machine or other ancillary services. Even when P2PM merchants move to a proper merchant, they continue to receive transactions up to Rs 2,000 without any charges or cap.
Article Summary: The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed. NPCI expects Rs 13,000-15,000 crore in the first year, with 5% of this being ploughed back to support small merchants.

Domestic and foreign institutional investors of Fortis Healthcare (Fortis) have expressed concern that the Delhi High Court ’s order seeking a forensic audit of transactions involving its former promoters, Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, could create a reputational overhang and weigh on investor confidence.The Aug 31 high court order came in a case arising from Japanese firm Daiichi Sankyo’s efforts to enforce its arbitral award against the erstwhile Fortis promoters. Last week, Fortis filed a special leave petition (SLP) in the Supreme Court challenging the order.Together, domestic and foreign institutional investors hold over half -- 57% shareholding, while the retail share is over 11% in the company.``The question for the market is whether a transaction that has cleared the entire approval architecture — board, shareholders, CCI, SEBI, the Takeover Code, ever becomes settled’’, Shriram Subramanian MD and founder of InGovern, a proxy advisory firm, told TOI.In 2018, Malaysia's IHH Healthcare acquired a controlling 31.1% stake in Fortis for approximately Rs 4,000 crore.``Questioning a transaction long cleared by all regulators and seeking its forensic audit after nearly a decade, will open a can of worms’’, he added.IHH is a credible strategic investor, and Fortis, after years of promoter-related turmoil and uncertainty, is now on a more stable footing, investors feel, and prolonged legal proceedings could create uncertainty.While the court has made clear that the forensic audit is a fact-finding exercise and does not, by itself, impose liability, investors said the process could still have wider implications for the company.``Capital is mobile and investors have alternatives; prolonged uncertainty can therefore have consequences for the company and its shareholders’’, InGovern said in a note, shared with TOI.The acquisition was approved by the board, cleared by the CCI, and completed under the SEBI Takeover Regulations through an open offer SEBI itself permitted. Neither IHH nor Fortis was a party to the arbitration, the award or the execution proceedings.Investors are also concerned about the possibility of the company being drawn into the matter at a later stage, including through the doctrine of “reverse veil piercing”.The company has also challenged this in its special leave petition arguing that reverse piercing, under which a company’s assets could potentially be subjected to the personal debts or obligations of its (erstwhile) controlling shareholder, has not been recognised by Indian courts.
Article Summary: The Delhi High Court’s order seeking a forensic audit of transactions involving its former promoters, Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, could create a reputational overhang and weigh on investor confidence. Last week, Fortis filed a special leave petition (SLP) in the Supreme Court challenging the order. In 2018, Malaysia's IHH Healthcare acquired a controlling 31.1% stake in Fortis for approximately Rs 4,000 crore.

NEW DELHI: Pakistan needs to take credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world can believe what it says, the ministry of external affairs said on Tuesday, while hitting out at Islamabad over its claims regarding a recent decision by the Permanent Court of Arbitration.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal accused Pakistan of “misrepresenting facts” and spreading “falsehoods” as part of its propaganda.“Pakistan has a habit of misrepresenting facts and propagating falsehoods to serve its malicious propaganda,” Jaiswal said.“For starters, the so-called ruling is not a ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration, as sought to be projected by the Pakistan minister. It is a ruling by an illegally constituted court. We see this as just one more attempt by Pakistan at distorting the reality,” he added.Jaiswal was responding to a question about Pakistan circulating a letter to the president of the UN Security Council regarding recent rulings related to the Permanent Court of Arbitration.His comments also came days after Pakistan increased the reward for information leading to the arrest or conviction of Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar.India had last week described Pakistan's PKR 70 lakh reward for information on Azhar as a “phoney” move and asked Islamabad to take concrete action against the JeM chief.The Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed has been linked to several major terror attacks in India, including the 2001 Parliament attack and the attacks in Pathankot and Pulwama.The group was founded by most-wanted terrorist Masood Azhar.New Delhi has repeatedly called on Pakistan to take credible action against crossborder terrorism, saying Islamabad's actions would be a key test of the credibility of its claims.On India-Bangladesh relations, Jaiswal said New Delhi wants positive and constructive ties with Dhaka.“India seeks positive, constructive and forward-looking ties with Bangladesh,” he said.On Indians missing in Nepal floods, Jaiswal said an Indian forensic team was working with Nepalese authorities to identify those still unaccounted for.“As I told you last time, we had given you a figure of 275 Indian nationals who were missing. Over and above that, several other people from the Indian diaspora and persons of Indian origin are also missing,” he said.“We have a forensic team in Nepal that is working in Kathmandu in several laboratories along with their Nepali colleagues,” Jaiswal said.He said the Indian team was working on 3,000 samples and had so far arrived at more than 1,200 DNA profiles.“The work is going on, and regarding the missing Indian nationals and missing persons, we await to hear from the Nepali authorities,” he said.On the Ukraine conflict, Jaiswal said external affairs minister S Jaishankar met Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha on Monday and discussed recent developments.“Yes, the external affairs minister met with the Ukrainian foreign minister yesterday. During the meeting, he discussed the recent developments in the conflict,” Jaiswal said.Jaishankar reiterated India's position that dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward for a peaceful resolution.“The external affairs minister once again put forth India's point that dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward for a peaceful resolution,” Jaiswal said.“India, as you know, is in touch with both sides, Ukraine and Russia, and we have told them that if there is any way that India can contribute, India is ready to do so,” he added.
Article Summary: Pakistan needs to take credible action against cross-border terrorism, India says. India accuses Pakistan of spreading "falsehoods" as part of its propaganda. India wants positive and constructive ties with Bangladesh. India working with Nepalese authorities to identify those still unaccounted for.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday questioned the steep markup on essential cancer medicines, with the bench describing the practice as “broad daylight dacoity” against patients. The remarks came after the court was informed that an essential cancer drug had a maximum retail price (MRP) of Rs 27,000, even though its price to retailers (PTR) was Rs 2,700, a tenfold difference.“There are essential medicines for cancer on which the MRP is printed as Rs 27,000 while the PTR is Rs 2,700. This is absolute rampage and carnage. This is broad daylight dacoity with patients,” news agency PTI quoted a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta saying.“It is very surprising that the authorities who are supposed to take action on this are silent,” it saidThe bench said the price gap was “absolutely shocking” and questioned how such pricing could be allowed.“The MRP is 10 times the rate at which it is provided to the retailers. If this is not extortion, then what it is? People sell their houses, ornaments to get treatment,” the bench said.The observations were made while the court was hearing two petitions dealing with drug-related issues, including demands for tighter price controls.One of the petitioners also raised the issue of registered medical practitioners prescribing generic medicines, and stressed the need for greater regulation of medicine prices.Additional solicitor general K M Nataraj, appearing for the Centre in one of the cases, told the court that the government was not approaching the litigation as an adversarial matter.The bench said fixing medicine prices remained a major concern and adjourned the matter to September 29.One of the petitions seeks measures to make drug formulations more affordable by preventing alleged unethical pricing of essential medicines by pharmaceutical companies and retailers. It also seeks strict enforcement of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, to check violations of price-control rules and disproportionate retailer margins.The other petition seeks disciplinary action against doctors for not prescribing generic medicines to patients.
Article Summary: Supreme Court raises concerns over steep pricing of essential cancer medicines. Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said the price gap was ‘absolutely shocking’ The bench said fixing medicine prices remained a major concern and adjourned the matter to September 29.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Govt is weighing the pros and cons of allowing Adani Group, which operates Mumbai airport, to run an airline. The Delhi and Mumbai airports went the PPP way in 2006 and their “operation, management and development agreement” (OMDA) does not allow the operators to have beyond 10% stake in an airline. Recently the Adani Group had sought amendment to the same.“Govt is clear that India needs more airlines, given the number of airports going to come up in India and the demand. Our ambition is to have at least five airlines with at least 100 aircraft each. So if someone wants to start an airline, govt supports the idea. The issue is an airport (Mumbai and Delhi) doing so. We are examining the pros and cons of the same,” Union aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said here Tuesday.Naidu said no decision on the Adani request has been taken so far. “We need to create a system where the cons (of allowing such a move) are taken care of. Pros we know. As such in govt there is no clause or rule anywhere which stops airport operators from having airlines other than the OMDA agreement for Delhi and Mumbai. If let us say BIAL (Bengaluru operator), which is still a private operator, wants to operate an airline, there is no rule stopping him.That’s why we have to take a balanced approach,” said Naidu.Adani’s request has divided the airline industry with IndiGo promoter Rahul Bhatia opposing the move and Akasa founder Vinay Dube being in favour of the same.The minister spoke about other issues at an UDAN event here Tuesday. “The aviation ministry, Airports Authority of India and 21 States & UTs (have) come together and sign MoUs to put a greater focus on speed, sustainability and long-term viability of projects in the next phase of UDAN… 100 airports will be developed under challenge mode over the next 10 years,” Naidu said.The cash-strapped airline’s woes have been mounting and its passengers often suffer delays running in several hours. “We are closely monitoring SpiceJet’s operations and finances through the aviation ⁠regulatory body to ensure safety is not compromised. Operational and financial scrutiny is being done. SpiceJet got Rs 150 crore under ECLGS. Getting more funds is something the airline has to work with banks with. It is a private airline. Our priority is to ensure passengers don’t face inconvenience and that safety is not compromised,” Naidu said.“The intention of the ministry is that all pilots must get tested within a year. The framework for the same has to be issued by the regulator DGCA. We have given our intent to them and they are holding deliberation with stakeholders. The DGCA rule change to ensure this is expected,” said the minister.Airfares will not be capped this festive season and the aviation ministry will advise airlines to keep the same at reasonable levels, said the minister. The hike being seen in recent dues is not due to the spike in demand but due to increased jet fuel prices.“We engage with airlines continuously and have regular meetings with them. And we definitely point it out to them that during this festive season, you have to ensure that the fair prices are kept at a reasonable level so that the people who want to travel, especially in these important times, get to see the benefit,” the minister said.
Article Summary: The Delhi and Mumbai airports went the PPP way in 2006 and their “operation, management and development agreement’ (OMDA) does not allow the operators to have beyond 10% stake in an airline. Recently the Adani Group had sought amendment to the same. “Govt is clear that India needs more airlines, given the number of airports going to come up in India and the demand,” said the minister.

DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on tuesday chaired a meeting of the State-Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee constituted for the effective implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and directed officials to ensure time-bound disposal of pending cases.Reviewing cases registered under the Act since 2024 where investigations are still pending, Dhami directed officials to examine the reasons for delays and take action on priority. He also called for close coordination among the police, administration and prosecution departments in long-pending and serious cases.The chief minister directed regular review of cases pending before special courts and asked officials to ensure the availability of special public prosecutors wherever required for effective prosecution.Dhami stressed that there should be no delay in disbursing prescribed relief to victims. He directed officials to separately review cases where relief payments have been delayed and said assistance to affected families should also extend, wherever required, to healthcare, education, security, rehabilitation and other eligible government schemes.The chief minister also directed officials to accord the highest priority to the safety of victims and their families in serious and sensitive cases.He said the education of children from affected families should not be disrupted and that eligible children should be linked with scholarships and other educational assistance schemes.According to the Social Welfare Department, the state has provisions for financial assistance to victims of atrocities under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, with assistance provided at different stages depending on the nature of the offence.Dhami further directed senior-level accountability in every district for monitoring cases under the Act and called for regular training of police personnel on its provisions, investigation of sensitive cases and appropriate conduct towards victims.He also instructed the Social Welfare, Police and Prosecution departments to jointly organise refresher training programmes and directed officials to work towards developing a digital monitoring system to track investigations, court proceedings, relief payments and other assistance.Districts where progress in investigation, disposal of cases or distribution of relief is unsatisfactory should be reviewed separately, Dhami said, adding that effective practices followed by better-performing districts should be shared with others.The chief minister also called for extensive awareness campaigns in rural and remote areas about the provisions of the Act, legal rights and assistance available to victims. He stressed that decisions taken during the meeting should not remain confined to official records and that responsibility and timelines should be fixed for every decision.The meeting was informed that 189 cases were registered under the Act in 2024 and 157 in 2025. In 2026, 116 cases had been registered up to September 15, of which 25 were under investigation.It was further informed that during 2024-25, financial assistance of Rs 228.71 lakh was provided to 205 victims; during 2025-26, Rs 143.16 lakh was provided to 127 victims; and during 2026-27, Rs 99.528 lakh had been provided to 104 victims as of September 18.Regular meetings have also been held at the state level under the chairmanship of the chief secretary and at the district level under the chairmanship of district magistrates.
Article Summary: Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday chaired a meeting of the State-Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee constituted for the effective implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989. The chief minister directed regular review of cases pending before special courts and asked officials to ensure availability of special public prosecutors.

Article Title: 'Naxalites can't make law': Heated exchange between lawyers during Vande Mataram SC hearing
Article Text:
SC hearing on Vande Mataram turns heated over 'Naxalites' remark
